raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Multi-turn multimodal RL on `/inference/v1/generate`: by turn N the prompt holds earlier images already expanded (from the previous response's `prompt_token_ids` / `mm_placeholders`) plus a new image with a compact placeholder. Today the request has to pick one of two mutually exclusive inputs, and neither fits:

- `content_parts` only: the processor matches the first placeholder tokens it finds, which sit inside the earlier expanded runs, so the prompt is silently corrupted unless the caller collapses every earlier run first.
- `features` only: the new image has no processed data.

As discussed below with @DarkLight1337 and @hickeyma, this PR lets the two be used together instead of detecting expansion in the processor (the earlier version of this PR):

- `features` carries the earlier items, already expanded, at explicit ranges.
- `content_parts` carries the new media. Only the prompt after the last `features` range is rendered, so the matcher never sees the expanded runs; its placeholders are shifted past that prefix and appended to the `features` items.

A new placeholder placed before the last `features` range is not in the rendered part, so it cannot be matched and the request gets a 400. The only processor change turns that unmatched-item `assert` (a 500) into a `VLLMValidationError`. Requests that use only one of the two fields behave as before.

## Why this is not a duplicate

Searched open PRs for `content_parts features`, `generate multimodal features`, `mm_placeholders generate`. #53169 reprocesses raw images to shrink payloads and does not combine the two inputs. #54548 (keep `is_embed` across the round trip) is orthogonal; until it lands, `features` items lose `is_embed` as they already do today.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_multimodal_tokens.py -v
```

`test_features_with_content_parts` renders a two-image prompt, then sends the first image as `features` and the second as `content_parts` with its placeholder collapsed, and checks that `/generate` returns the same `prompt_token_ids` and `mm_placeholders` as `/render`. On main this request is rejected (`content_parts and features are mutually exclusive`).

## Test Result

Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct on 1x GB200 in the `vllm/vllm-openai` nightly image (`18f8f96`, with this diff applied to its copies of the changed files): `6 passed`. Without the change, `test_features_with_content_parts` fails (400 Bad Request).

AI assistance (Claude) was used; I reviewed every changed line.

> We intentionally removed this in #53385 in order to simplify the processing code. Is calling the Renderer API separately to pre-process the prompt not an option for RL?


Thanks, I missed 53385.

The Renderer has a gap for multi-turn RL:
- `/v1/chat/completions/render` follows the Chat protocol: images go in message content parts, but the input is messages only, with no way to pass token IDs.
- `/v1/completions/render` follows the legacy Completions protocol: `prompt` is text or token IDs, with no content parts, so there is nowhere to put an image.

RL needs both: the tokens sampled in earlier turns must be kept exactly, and later turns can bring new images. That leaves only chat render, so the caller either re-renders the whole conversation (detokenize then retokenize, which is not guaranteed to round-trip) or splices tokens and shifts offsets itself.

Separately, an expanded prompt sent back as-is is still silently expanded a second time (128 -> 255), and with #57781 closed nothing catches it.

Two low-cost options:
1. An explicit flag: when the request says the prompt is already expanded, only locate placeholders and skip expansion. The default path costs one boolean check.
2. A local check: when the matcher hits the first placeholder, look at the next token to see whether it is still a placeholder, without scanning the whole prompt.

what do you think?

I think both of these solutions are suboptimal as it implies redundant processing (tokenization for (1), prompt scanning for (2)).

Perhaps a better solution would be to accept `prompt_token_ids` alongside multimodal inputs as suggested by #55770.

cc @shijie-lyu @hickeyma

> I think both of these solutions are suboptimal as it implies redundant processing (tokenization for (1), prompt scanning for (2)).
Perhaps a better solution would be to accept prompt_token_ids alongside multimodal inputs as suggested by https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55770.
cc @shijie-lyu @hickeyma

I agree that a request level contract is better than having the processor guess. One thing though. `/inference/v1/generate` already takes `token_ids` + `content_parts` and that's where this bug shows up. So adding `prompt_token_ids` + media to chat completions would run into the same problem. What we actually need to decide is whether those ids are compact or expanded.

If they're compact, RL callers still have to collapse the expanded runs back to one placeholder (dedup) themselves, like OpenRLHF/verl/TRL do today. If they forget, the prompt gets corrupted without any error. If they're expanded, we need "find the placeholders, don't expand" and that's what this PR does.

The `features` path on generate already takes expanded ids, so maybe the smaller change is letting `features` (earlier turns) work together with `content_parts` (new media in later turns), instead of keeping them mutually exclusive. Then RL stays on tokens-in and chat completions doesn't need a new field. 

What do people think?
I prefer avoiding changes to OpenAI endpoints if we could instead adjust `/inference/v1/generate` so that it can continue to be used for RL

> I prefer avoiding changes to OpenAI endpoints if we could instead adjust `/inference/v1/generate` so that it can continue to be used for RL

Agree, didn't expect this pr would affect all endpoints.

+1 to @hickeyma's proposal: let `features` (earlier turns) and `content_parts` (new media) be used together on `/inference/v1/generate`. Two things the implementation needs to get right:

1. Matching for the new items must skip the ranges declared in `features`. Otherwise a new image binds to the first placeholder token it finds, which can sit inside an earlier image's expanded run, and we are back to silent corruption.
2. Expanding a new item shifts everything after it. Either shift the declared `features` offsets (and return the final `mm_placeholders`), or require new items to come after all declared ranges and reject otherwise. RL appends, so the second option is enough.

If this direction works for everyone, I'll close this PR and rework it along these lines.
Let's see what you come up with
Go for it @aoshen02
Documentation preview: https://vllm--57796.org.readthedocs.build/en/57796/

> I think both of these solutions are suboptimal as it implies redundant processing (tokenization for (1), prompt scanning for (2)).
> 
> Perhaps a better solution would be to accept `prompt_token_ids` alongside multimodal inputs as suggested by #55770.
> 
> cc @shijie-lyu @hickeyma

Thanks for the cc. +1 to keeping this on `/inference/v1/generate`.

One constraint for anyone revisiting token ids plus media on chat completions: with prompt_token_ids set, chat currently rejects non-text content (#59173). A token-only prompt carries no multimodal hashes, so its cached blocks would collide with any other prompt of the same text. Supporting both there would need the placeholder ranges and hashes that features already carries, so /generate is the better place. #55770 stays text-only.

@@ -70,6 +70,51 @@ The final output of every choice carries `weight_versions`, the label of the wei
 - An output with no tokens, such as a request aborted before its first token, gets `[]`.
 - The labels are the ones you set with `/update_weight_version` or `/finish_weight_update`, see [Async Reinforcement Learning](../../training/async_rl.md#weight-versions-in-outputs). vLLM doesn't order or check them, and the label is `"default"` until you set one.
 
+## Multimodal inputs
+
+A request can carry media in two ways, and can use both at once:
+
+- `content_parts`: raw media (`image_url`, `audio_url` or `video_url`, each with an optional `uuid`). `token_ids` holds one placeholder token per item, and the server expands it.
+- `features`: items whose placeholders are already expanded in `token_ids`, at the ranges given in `mm_placeholders`. Pass the processed tensors in `kwargs_data`, or omit them to look the items up in the processor cache by `mm_hashes`.
+
+When both are set, every `content_parts` placeholder must come after the last `features` range. Only the tokens after that range are processed, so the expanded runs before it are left as they are. Models that insert media at the start of the prompt (such as PaliGemma, BLIP-2 and Molmo) would place a new item right after that range without an error, so don't combine the two fields for them.
+
+This fits multi-turn rollouts. Each turn resends the previous prompt with its images already expanded, adds the new turn with one placeholder per new image, and sends the earlier images as `features`:
+
+```python
+import httpx
+
+url = "http://localhost:8000/inference/v1/generate"
+
+# Turn 1: turn1_ids holds one <|image_pad|> for image A.
+turn1 = httpx.post(url, json={
+    "token_ids": turn1_ids,
+    "content_parts": [{"type": "image_url", "url": url_a, "uuid": "img-a"}],
+    "sampling_params": {"max_tokens": 256},
+    "return_token_ids": True,
+}).json()
+
+# Turn 2: image A is expanded in turn1["prompt_token_ids"];
+# turn2_ids appends one <|image_pad|> for image B.
+turn2 = httpx.post(url, json={
+    "token_ids": (
+        turn1["prompt_token_ids"] + turn1["choices"][0]["token_ids"] + turn2_ids
+    ),
+    "features": {
+        "mm_hashes": {"image": ["img-a"]},
+        "mm_placeholders": turn1["mm_placeholders"],
+    },
+    "content_parts": [{"type": "image_url", "url": url_b, "uuid": "img-b"}],
+    "sampling_params": {"max_tokens": 256},
+    "return_token_ids": True,
+}).json()
+```
+
+Here `"img-a"` finds image A in the processor cache because turn 1 sent it with that `uuid`. Two cases need a different approach:
+
+- If the server sets `--mm-processor-kwargs` or `--media-io-kwargs`, the `uuid` is hashed with them and is no longer the cache key. Take `features` from a [render](renderer.md) response instead.
+- If the item has been evicted from the cache, the request fails. Resend the item with `kwargs_data`.
+
 ## Aborting requests
 
 `POST /inference/v1/abort_requests` aborts in-flight requests. It is registered wherever `/inference/v1/generate` is and requires the API key when `--api-key` is set, like `/inference/v1/generate`.

+## Multimodal inputs
+
+A request can carry media in two ways, and can use both at once:
+
+- `content_parts`: raw media (`image_url`, `audio_url` or `video_url`, each with an optional `uuid`). `token_ids` holds one placeholder token per item, and the server expands it.
+- `features`: items whose placeholders are already expanded in `token_ids`, at the ranges given in `mm_placeholders`. Pass the processed tensors in `kwargs_data`, or omit them to look the items up in the processor cache by `mm_hashes`.

+## Multimodal inputs
+
+A request can carry media in two ways, and can use both at once:
+
+- `content_parts`: raw media (`image_url`, `audio_url` or `video_url`, each with an optional `uuid`). `token_ids` holds one placeholder token per item, and the server expands it.
+- `features`: items whose placeholders are already expanded in `token_ids`, at the ranges given in `mm_placeholders`. Pass the processed tensors in `kwargs_data`, or omit them to look the items up in the processor cache by `mm_hashes`.
+
+When both are set, every `content_parts` placeholder must come after the last `features` range. Only the tokens after that range are processed, so the expanded runs before it are left as they are.
+
+This fits multi-turn rollouts. Each turn resends the previous prompt with its images already expanded, adds the new turn with one placeholder per new image, and sends the earlier images as `features`:
+
+```python
+import httpx
+
+url = "http://localhost:8000/inference/v1/generate"
+
+# Turn 1: turn1_ids holds one <|image_pad|> for image A.
+turn1 = httpx.post(url, json={
+    "token_ids": turn1_ids,
+    "content_parts": [{"type": "image_url", "url": url_a, "uuid": "img-a"}],
+    "sampling_params": {"max_tokens": 256},
+    "return_token_ids": True,
+}).json()
+
+# Turn 2: image A is expanded in turn1["prompt_token_ids"];
+# turn2_ids appends one <|image_pad|> for image B.
+turn2 = httpx.post(url, json={
+    "token_ids": (
+        turn1["prompt_token_ids"] + turn1["choices"][0]["token_ids"] + turn2_ids
+    ),
+    "features": {
+        "mm_hashes": {"image": ["img-a"]},
+        "mm_placeholders": turn1["mm_placeholders"],
+    },
+    "content_parts": [{"type": "image_url", "url": url_b, "uuid": "img-b"}],
+    "sampling_params": {"max_tokens": 256},
+    "return_token_ids": True,
+}).json()
+```
+
+Here `"img-a"` finds image A in the processor cache because turn 1 sent it with that `uuid`. Two cases need a different approach:
+
+- If the server sets `--mm-processor-kwargs` or `--media-io-kwargs`, the `uuid` is hashed with them and is no longer the cache key. Take `features` from a [render](renderer.md) response instead.

We intentionally removed this in #53385 in order to simplify the processing code. Is calling the Renderer API separately to pre-process the prompt not an option for RL?

> We intentionally removed this in #53385 in order to simplify the processing code. Is calling the Renderer API separately to pre-process the prompt not an option for RL?


Thanks, I missed 53385.

The Renderer has a gap for multi-turn RL:
- `/v1/chat/completions/render` follows the Chat protocol: images go in message content parts, but the input is messages only, with no way to pass token IDs.
- `/v1/completions/render` follows the legacy Completions protocol: `prompt` is text or token IDs, with no content parts, so there is nowhere to put an image.

RL needs both: the tokens sampled in earlier turns must be kept exactly, and later turns can bring new images. That leaves only chat render, so the caller either re-renders the whole conversation (detokenize then retokenize, which is not guaranteed to round-trip) or splices tokens and shifts offsets itself.

Separately, an expanded prompt sent back as-is is still silently expanded a second time (128 -> 255), and with #57781 closed nothing catches it.

Two low-cost options:
1. An explicit flag: when the request says the prompt is already expanded, only locate placeholders and skip expansion. The default path costs one boolean check.
2. A local check: when the matcher hits the first placeholder, look at the next token to see whether it is still a placeholder, without scanning the whole prompt.

what do you think?

I think both of these solutions are suboptimal as it implies redundant processing (tokenization for (1), prompt scanning for (2)).

Perhaps a better solution would be to accept `prompt_token_ids` alongside multimodal inputs as suggested by #55770.

cc @shijie-lyu @hickeyma

> I think both of these solutions are suboptimal as it implies redundant processing (tokenization for (1), prompt scanning for (2)).
Perhaps a better solution would be to accept prompt_token_ids alongside multimodal inputs as suggested by https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55770.
cc @shijie-lyu @hickeyma

I agree that a request level contract is better than having the processor guess. One thing though. `/inference/v1/generate` already takes `token_ids` + `content_parts` and that's where this bug shows up. So adding `prompt_token_ids` + media to chat completions would run into the same problem. What we actually need to decide is whether those ids are compact or expanded.

If they're compact, RL callers still have to collapse the expanded runs back to one placeholder (dedup) themselves, like OpenRLHF/verl/TRL do today. If they forget, the prompt gets corrupted without any error. If they're expanded, we need "find the placeholders, don't expand" and that's what this PR does.

The `features` path on generate already takes expanded ids, so maybe the smaller change is letting `features` (earlier turns) work together with `content_parts` (new media in later turns), instead of keeping them mutually exclusive. Then RL stays on tokens-in and chat completions doesn't need a new field. 

What do people think?
I prefer avoiding changes to OpenAI endpoints if we could instead adjust `/inference/v1/generate` so that it can continue to be used for RL

> I prefer avoiding changes to OpenAI endpoints if we could instead adjust `/inference/v1/generate` so that it can continue to be used for RL

Agree, didn't expect this pr would affect all endpoints.

+1 to @hickeyma's proposal: let `features` (earlier turns) and `content_parts` (new media) be used together on `/inference/v1/generate`. Two things the implementation needs to get right:

1. Matching for the new items must skip the ranges declared in `features`. Otherwise a new image binds to the first placeholder token it finds, which can sit inside an earlier image's expanded run, and we are back to silent corruption.
2. Expanding a new item shifts everything after it. Either shift the declared `features` offsets (and return the final `mm_placeholders`), or require new items to come after all declared ranges and reject otherwise. RL appends, so the second option is enough.

If this direction works for everyone, I'll close this PR and rework it along these lines.
Let's see what you come up with

> I think both of these solutions are suboptimal as it implies redundant processing (tokenization for (1), prompt scanning for (2)).
> 
> Perhaps a better solution would be to accept `prompt_token_ids` alongside multimodal inputs as suggested by #55770.
> 
> cc @shijie-lyu @hickeyma

Thanks for the cc. +1 to keeping this on `/inference/v1/generate`.

One constraint for anyone revisiting token ids plus media on chat completions: with prompt_token_ids set, chat currently rejects non-text content (#59173). A token-only prompt carries no multimodal hashes, so its cached blocks would collide with any other prompt of the same text. Supporting both there would need the placeholder ranges and hashes that features already carries, so /generate is the better place. #55770 stays text-only.
